चक्र: Cakra m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Vāsuki, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacri-fice of Janamejaya 1. 52. 5.
चक्रमन्द: Cakramanda m.: A mythical serpent. One of those who received the white snake issuing from the mouth of Balarāma and entering the ocean 16. 5. 15, 12.
चण्डतुण्डक: Caṇḍatuṇḍaka m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 9. 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रीवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because destroying his kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
चन्द्रक: Candraka m.: An owl. Had a sharp beak and quick-moving eyes; he threatened the life of the mouse, Palita; the mouse requested the cat, Lomaśa, to protect him from the owl; when the mouse was safe with the cat, the owl left for his dwelling place 12. 136. 32, 53, 73, 82, 112, 114.
चिकुर: Cikura m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Airāvata; son of Āryaka; father of Sumukha; he was killed and eaten up by Vainateya (Garuḍa) 5. 101. 24; 5. 102. 12, 14.
चित्र: Citra m.: A mythical serpent. One of the snakes who without fatigue wait upon Varuṇa in his सभा; strong, marked with banner (पताकिन्), and round spots (मण्डलिन्), hooded (फणवन्त्) 2. 9. 8, 10; one of the two big snakes (महा-नागौ), the other being Airāvata, shaken on hearing the roar of Skanda; both held by Skanda in his two hands when he saw them approaching to attack him 3. 214. 22-23.
चित्रबर्ह: Citrabarha m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99, 12, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on ser-pents; marked with श्रीवत्स, Viṣṇu is his deity; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brahminhood because indulging in killing kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
चित्रवेदिक: Citravedika m.: A mythical serpent. Born in the कुल of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, listed by Sūta among those offered in the snake sacrifice of Janamejaya; described as ‘fast as wind’ (वातवेग), ‘having excess of poison’ (विषोल्बण) 1. 52. 17, 13.
चित्रसेन: Citrasena m.: A mythical serpent. Son of Kadrū, poisonous and easily angered (मुहारोष); he sided with Arjuna when those who gathered in the mid-region to watch the battle took sides between Karṇa and Arjuna 8. 63. 36.
चिरान्तक: Cirāntaka m.: A mythical bird, living in the world of Suparṇas 5. 99. 13, 1. Born in the कुल of Vainateya (Garuḍa), in the वंश of Kaśyapa; feeding on serpents; marked with श्रिवत्स, his deity is Viṣṇu; by action a Kṣatriya, not obtaining Brāhminhood because indulging in destroying kinsmen 5. 99. 2-8.
चक्रव्यूह: Cakravyūha m.: Name of a व्यूह (a particular arrangement of the army). Droṇa arranged the Kaurava army according to this व्यूह on the thirteenth day of the war. A. Description: impenetrable (दुर्-भिद) 7. 32. 18; impenetrable even for the gods (अभेद्यस् त्रिदशैर् अपि) 7. 32. 13; unassailable (अनाधृष्य) 7. 34. 1; difficult to look at, when it moved it shone like the mid-day sun (चरन् मध्यंदिने सूर्यः प्रपतन्न् इव दुर्दृशः) 7. 32. 17. B. Arrangement: A special force of ten thousand kings (राजानः 7. 33. 12; संघातो राजपुत्राणां 7. 33. 13) fighting with strong bows under the leader-ship of Lakṣmaṇa (son of Duryodhana) was employed in it; they were comparable with Indra, had golden banners with red flags, dressed in red robes, and wearing red decora-tions and gold strings; they had formed a cove-nant (कृताभिसमयाः 7. 33. 13); they shared their grief with each other, they were of equal daring and they vied with each other (in this regard), and were intent on each other's well-being (अन्योन्यसमदुःखास् ते अन्यो-न्यसमसाहसाः । अन्योन्यं स्पर्धमानाश् च अन्योन्यस्य हिते रताः 7. 33. 16); Dur-yodhana, surrounded by Karṇa, Duḥśāsana and Kṛpa was also involved in it; Droṇa and Jayadratha stood at the head of the army (प्रमुखे 7. 33. 18); thirty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with Aśvatthāman to lead them, stood on one side of Jayadratha and on the other stood Śakuni, Śalya and Bhūriśravas 7. 33. 12-20. C. Abhimanyu agreed to penetrate the Cakravyūha: Penetrating the व्यूह was a task difficult to be ac-complished 7. 32. 19 (दुष्करं कर्म), a burden difficult to bear (अविषह्यं गुरुं भारम्) 7. 34. 12; its penetration (भेद) not known to any one except Kṛṣṇa, Arjuna, Pradyumna and Abhimanyu; even Abhi-manyu was taught by Arjuna the way to enter it, but not the way to get out of it in case of emergency (नोत्सहे तु विनिर्-गन्तुम् अहं कस्यांचिद् आपदि) 7. 34. 14-15, 19; 7. 50. 20-21; Abhimanyu commis-sioned by Yudhiṣṭhira to penetrate the व्यूह and the Pāṇḍavas assured him of support from the rear 7. 34. 16-17; 20-23, 7. 32. 18; (subsequently when Abhimanyu entered it and was isolated from the other Pāṇḍavas by Jayadratha, he was killed while fighting).
चक्रशकट: Cakraśakaṭa, Śakaṭa m.: Name of a व्यूह (a particular arrangement of the army; also called for short Śakaṭa) 7. 63. 26, 28; 7. 65. 2; 7. 53. 27. A. Description: Constituetd of a con-centration of many chariots, foot-soldiers, horses, and elephants; the व्यूह looked like an agitated sea; it appeared as if it could swallow the entire earth with mountains, oceans and forests, and different peoples (जनपद); it was capable of striking terror in the hearts of the enemies 7. 63. 31-33; called महाव्यूह (7. 63. 24); it was twelve गव्यूतिस् long and five गव्यूतिस् wide in the rear half (7. 63. 21). B. Arrangement: In the interior of the rear half, a section of the army was arranged to form Padmavyūha which was difficult to penetrate (पश्चार्धे तस्य पद्मस् तु गर्-भव्यूहः सुदुर्भिदः 7. 63. 23; 7. 53. 27; concealed (गूढः) within the Padma-vyūha there was yet another व्यूह known as Sūcī 7. 63. 23; at the entrance (मुख) of the main Cakraśakaṭavyūha stood Droṇa himself with the king of the Bhojas to offer protection to him 7. 63. 28-29; in the front of all the army divisions (अग्रटः सर्वसैन्-यानाम् 7. 63. 19) stood Durmarṣaṇa, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, with a thousand and five hundred fierce elephants mounted by skilled fighters; Durmarṣaṇa was accompanied by his brothers Duḥśāsana and Vikarṇa (they were अग्रानीके व्यवस्थितौ) to guard the interests of Jayadratha 7. 63. 19-20; at the entrance (मुख) of the Sūcīvyūha stood ready Kṛtavarman, followed by the Kām-bhoja king and king Jalasandha; they were supported by Duryodhana and his ministers (सहामात्यः 7. 63. 25); behind them all were stationed, to protect the Sūcivyūha, hundreds and thousands of warriors who would never turn back while fighting (योधानाम् अनिवर्तिनाम् 7. 63. 26); behind them, at the position of the ‘eye of the needle’ (सूचिपाशे) of the Sūcīvyūha stood Jayadratha surrounded by a large force 7. 63. 27; 7. 53. 27; he was guarded by six principal warriors, Saumadatti (Bhūriśravas), Karṇa, Aśvatthāman, Śalya, Vṛṣasena, Kṛpa, with a force consisting of a hundred thou-sand horsemen, six अयुतस् of chariot-fighters, fourteen thousand elephant-riders, and twentyone thousand foot-soldiers; the place where Jayadratha was stationed was at a distance of three गव्यूतिस् from the main battle front where Droṇa stood guard 7. 63. 11-14; 7. 53. 26, 28. C. Purpose: The व्यूह was designed by Droṇa on the 14th day of the war to save Jayadratha from being killed by Arjuna 7. 63. 21, 22, 24, 15.
चन्द्रार्ध: Candrārdha m.: Name of a व्यूह (a particular arrangement of the army). The Saṃśaptakas arranged their army according to the व्यूह known as Candrārdha in which only the chariot-fighters were stationed in the front (व्यूह्यानीकं रथैर् एव); the army was stationed on level ground (समे देशे व्यवस्थिताः) 7. 17. 1. [See Ardhacandra]
चार्वाकनिग्रह: Cārvākanigraha m.: Name of the 84th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 63, 33, 70. Alluded to in 9. 63. 38; related to the incident told in the अध्यायस् 12. 39. 22-47.
चैत्ररथ: Caitraratha nt.: Name of the 11th पर्वन् in the list of a hundred sub-पर्वन्स् of the Bhārata supposed to have been made by Vyāsa in the Parvasaṃgraha 1. 2. 36, 33, 70. Referred to as the defeat of Aṅgāra-parṇa (अङ्गारपर्णं निर्जित्य) in the list of the contents of the Ādiparvan 1. 2. 86; the following अध्यायस् are considered to belong to the Caitrarathaparvan 1. 153-173; the actual encounter with Aṅgāraparṇa is found in the अध्याय 1. 158.

Caitraratha nt.: Name of the grove of Kubera (named after Citraratha, the king of the Gandharvas). A. Location: In the north (अत्र (i. e. अस्यां (उत्तरस्यां) दिशि 5. 109. 3) चैत्र-रथं रम्यम् 5. 109. 9; on the Śveta mountain 3. 214. 30, 34-35; 3. 215. 2. B. Epic events: (1) Pāṇḍu went to this grove from the Nāgasabha mountain and from there he proceeded further to the Hima-vant 1. 110. 43; (2) Kṛṣṇa performed here the Turāyaṇa and other sacrifices 3. 13. 21. C. Mythological event: People living in the Caitraratha were distressed when Skanda felled down the peak of the Śveta (3. 214. 34) 3. 215. 2. D. Similes: (1) Duḥṣanta saw a large forest on the river Mālinī which looked like the Caitraratha (महद् वनम् … चैत्र-रथप्रख्यम्) 1. 64. 24-25; (2) The large forest Viśākhayūpa on the Yāmuna mountain looked like the Caitraratha (चैत्र-रथप्रकाश 3. 174. 17, 20; (3) Indra saw women sporting in a forest near the town of Vṛṣaparvan which was comparable with the Caitraratha 1. 73. 4; (4) In the third inner enclosure (कक्ष्या) of the residence of Janaka (12. 312. 32), Śuka saw a large forest comparable with the Caitraratha 12. 312. 33; (5) When Karṇa vowed the death of Arjuna, Duryodhana, satisfied, entered the house as does the master (Citraratha ? Kubera ?) the Caitraratha (यथा चैत्ररथं प्रभुः) 3. 243. 17; (6) When Arjuna left the Kāmyaka forest it became like the Caitra-ratha devoid of Kubera 3. 79. 6; (7) The terrified army of the Kauravas stood motion-less like the Caitraratha grove covered with flowers (ततः सा शुशुभे सेना निश्चेष्टा-वस्थिता नृप । नानापुष्पसमाकीर्णम् यथा चैत्ररथं वनम्) 8. 37. 10.
चित्रा: Citrā f.: Name of a constellation. A. Religious rites: (1) Nārada told Devakī (13. 63. 2-4) that if one gave as a gift a bull and auspicious perfumes under Citrā (चित्रायाम्) one moved in the world of the Apsarases and enjoyed in the Nandana-vana 13. 63. 17; (2) Yama told Śaśabindu (13. 89. 1) that by offering a काम्य श्राद्ध under Citrā one got handsome sons 13. 89. 7. B. Bad omens: (1) Karṇa pointed out to Kṛṣṇa that the Kauravas were facing great danger because the planet (Mahāpāta) was severely afflicting Citrā (नूनं महद् भयं कृष्ण कुरूणां समुपस्थितम् । विशेषेण हि वार्ष्णेय चित्रां पीडयते ग्र-हः ॥ ) 5. 141. 9 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 5. 143. 10: चित्रां ग्रहो महापाताख्यो ज्योतिः-शास्त्रप्रसिद्धः । तेन राकारस्य वेधाद् राजजातीयानां क्षयो भवितेति भावः । ); (2) Among the bad omens pointed out by Vyāsa to Dhṛtarāṣṭra there was one according to which a Śvetagraha (also called a harsh ग्रह = Ketu) had gone beyond Citrā and was at the beginning of Svāti (श्वेतो ग्रहस् तथा चित्रां समतिक्रम्य तिष्ठति) 6. 3. 11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 6. 3. 12: श्वेतो ग्रहः केतुश् चित्राम् अतिक्रामति स्वात्यादौ वर्तते); (चित्रास्वात्यन्तरे चैव धिष्ठितः परुषो ग्रहः) 6. 3. 16.
चैत्र: Caitra m.: Name of a month. Aṅgiras had told Bhīṣma (13. 109. 9-10) that if one, with restrained mind, spent the month of Caitra eating only once a day he was born in a noted family that was rich with gold, gems and pearls 13. 109. 22; Nārada told the Pāṇḍavas that Brahmadeva and other gods, the Seers, the Siddhas and the Cāraṇas visit the famous and very holy con-fluence of the river Sarasvatī where Janārdana was worshipped (सङ्गमं लोकविश्रुतम् । सरस्वत्या महापुण्यम् उपासन्ते जनार्-दनम् ॥ 3. 80. 130) on the fourteenth day of the bright half of Caitra (3. 80. 131); if a king was threatened by a stronger adver-sary (12. 69. 32) he should, in the month of Caitra when there was fear of fire, get in advance all houses, that were covered with grass, smeared with mud and remove the grass from them (तृणच्छन्नानि वेश्मानि पङ्केनापि प्रलेपयेत् । निर्हरेच् च तृणं मासे चैत्रे वह्निभयात् पुरः) 12. 69. 45.
चैत्री: Caitrī f.; adj.: Name of the day of the full moon in the month of Caitra; occurring in Caitra. Vyāsa told Yudhiṣṭhira that he will be consecrated for the Aśvamedha sacrifice on the full moon day of Caitra (चैत्र्यां हि पौर्णमास्यां च तव दीक्षा भविष्यति) 14. 71. 4; after defeating Vajradatta, son of Bhagadatta of the Prāgjyotiṣa, Arjuna invited him to attend the Aśvamedha sacrifice of Dharmarāja which would take place on the following full moon day of Caitra (आगच्-छेत्था महाराज परां चैत्रीम् उपस्थि-ताम् । तदाश्वमेधो भविता धर्मराजस्य धीमतः) 14. 75. 25; he similarly invited Babhruvāhana 14. 82. 24, Meghasaṃdhi (grandson of Jarāsaṃdha, son of Sahadeva) 14. 83. 27, and Śakuni's son 14. 85. 23; marching out of an army for attack is re-commended on the full moon day of Caitra or Mārgaśīrṣa for the crops are then ripe and there is ample water; it is also then neither too hot nor too cold (चैत्र्यां वा मार्ग-शीर्ष्यां वा सेनायोगः प्रशस्यते । पक्व-सस्या हि पृथिवी भवत्य् अम्बुमती तथा ॥ नैवातिशीतो नात्युष्णः कालो भवति भारत । तस्मात् तदा योजयेत) 12. 101. 9-10.
चन्दना: Candanā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 28, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
चन्द्रभागा: Candrabhāgā f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 14, 13; one of the six rivers which flow outside the country called the Āraṭṭa (पञ्च नद्यो वहन्त्य् एताः  … आरट्टा नाम ते देशाः) 8. 30. 35-36. B. Description: Listed among the rivers which are described as most holy (पुण्यतमाः) and auspicious (शिवाः) 13. 134. 16, 22; excellent rivers (सरिद्वराः) 13. 134. 14, (सरिच्छ्रेष्ठाः) 13. 134. 22, containing waters of all the तीर्थस् (सर्वतीर्थोदकैर् युताः) 13. 134. 12, and flowing to the ocean (सागरगमाः) 13. 134. 21; the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for cita-tion see Atikṛṣṇā). C. Importance: (1) One of the rivers said to be expert in the duties of women (स्त्रीधर्मकुशलाः) 13. 134. 19; Umā wanted to consult them before expounding स्त्रीधर्म to Śiva 13. 134. 13, 18-21; (2) One of the rivers which wait upon Śiva for him to take bath (उपस्पर्शनहेतोः) 13. 134. 16, 12; (3) One of the rivers which, in bodily form (2. 9. 21), wait upon Varuṇa in his Sabhā 2. 9. 19; (4) One of the rivers seen by the sage Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārāyaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93; (5) Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 14. D. Holiness: He who, being free from attachment (निर्ममः), bathes in the Candrabhāgā for a week and observes fast becomes like a मुनि (मुनिवद् भवेत्) 13. 26. 7.
चन्द्रमसस्: Candramasas tīrtham nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। Situated on the Ārcīka mountain; it was worshipped (पर्युपासते) by sages, the Vaikhānasas and the Vālakhilyas 3. 125. 14.
चमस: Camasa, Camasodbheda (m.), Cama-sonmajjana nt.: Name of a तीर्थ। A. Location: Situated in the Surāṣṭras (सुराष्ट्रेषु) 3. 86. 16-17. B. Holy: One of the three तीर्थस् where the river Sarasvatī rises again after disappearing in the desert near the Vinaśanatīrtha 3. 80. 118; a तीर्थ where Sarasvatī can be seen; at this तीर्थ many divine and holy (rivers), flowing towards the ocean, turn towards the Sarasvatī (यत्र दृश्या सरस्वती । यत्रैनाम् अभ्यवर्तन्त दिव्याः पुण्याः समुद्रगाः) 3. 130. 5; by bathing at this तीर्थ one gets the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice 3. 80. 119. C. Epic event: Halāyudha (Bala-rāma) stayed there for a night, bathed in the तीर्थ according to the prescriptions, and gave many special gifts; from there he pro-ceeded to the Udapāna 9. 34. 78-80.
चम्पकारण्य: Campakāraṇya nt.: Name of a sacred forest. Described as best (उत्तम); by staying there for a night one gets the fruit of giving a thousands cows 3. 82. 114. [See Jyeṣṭhila]
चरक्षा: Carakṣā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 29, 13; all the rivers listed here are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
चर्मण्वती: Carmaṇvatī f.: Name of a river. A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 18, 13; Droṇa gave to Drupada the kingship of the Pāñcāla country to the south of the Bhāgī-rathī and extending up to the Carmaṇvatī (दक्षिणांश् चैव पाञ्चालान् यावच् चर्मण्-वती नदी) 1. 128. 15, 12; Sahadeva, pro-ceeding to the south of Indraprastha for his expedition (2. 28. 1) encountered Bhoja, the son of Jambhaka, on the bank of the Carmaṇ-vatī; he defeated him and then proceeded to the south (स तम् आजौ विनिर्जित्य दक्षिणा-भिमुखो ययौ) 2. 28. 7-8; Kṛṣṇa and the two Pāṇḍavas, while proceeding towards the Magadha country, went beyond Mithilā and reached the rivers Mālā and Carmaṇvatī (अतीत्य जग्मुर् मिथिलां मालां चर्मण्-वतीं नदीम्) 2. 18. 28. B. Name ex-plained: See section G below. C. Descrip-tion: Great river (महानदी) 12. 29. 116; all the rivers listed by Saṃjaya are described as mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā). D. Holiness: (1) He who is controlled and takes limited food (नियतो नियताशनः), if he visits the Carmaṇavatī, he gets, as permitted by Rantideva, the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma (रन्तिदेवाभ्यनुज्ञातो अग्निष्टोमफलं लभेत्) 3. 80. 73; (2) Listed by Mārkaṇ-ḍeya among the rivers which are proclaimed to be mothers of sacrificial hearths, i. e. on the banks of which sacrifices were performed (एता नद्यस् तु धिष्ण्यानां मातरो याः प्रकीर्तिताः 3. 212. 22, 24 (see Kapilā for Nī.). E. Importance: (1) Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 22, 2; (2) One of the rivers seen by Mārkaṇḍeya in the belly of the Bāla (3. 186. 83 = Nārā-yaṇa 3. 187. 3) 3. 186. 93. F. Epic events: (1) The basket containing the newly born Karṇa was put in the river Aśva-nadī; from there it went to the Carmaṇvatī, and further to Yamunā 3. 292. 25; (2-4); for the other three epic events related to this river see section A above. G. Past events: (1) The river flew from the dampness of the heap of the skins of cows offered in the sacri-fice of Rantideva; hence called Carmaṇvatī (महानदी चर्मराशेर् उत्क्लेदात् सुस्रुवे यतः । ततश् चर्मण्वतीत्य् एवं विख्याता सा महानदी ॥ ) 12. 29. 116; (रन्तिदेवस्य यज्ञे ताः पशुत्वेनोपकल्पिताः । ततश् चर्-मण्वती राजन् गोचर्मभ्यः प्रवर्तिता ॥ ) 13. 65. 41.
चान्द्रमस: Cāndramasa hrada m.: Name of a lake. From the summit of the mountain Meru Gaṅgā Bhāgīrathī fell down with terrific speed in the Cāndramasa lake; the lake was created by the falling Gaṅgā 6. 7. 26-27; described as auspicious (शुभ), holy (पुण्य) and as large as the sea (सागरो-पम) 6. 7. 27.
चित्रकूट: Citrakūṭa m.: Name of a mountain. Described as a great mountain (महा-गिरि) 3. 266. 67; best among excellent moun-tains (गिरिवरश्रेष्ठ) 3. 83. 55; the river Mandākinī flows on it 3. 83. 55; one who observes fast and bathes in the river Mandā-kinī gets the royal glory (राजलक्ष्मीं निगच्छति) 13. 26. 27; Bharata, searching Rāma to take him back to Ayodhyā, met him on this mountain 3. 261. 37; Sītā told Hanūmant that the incident when Rāma threw a reed (इषीका) at a crow occurred on the Citrakūṭa 3. 266. 67; mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 27, 2.
चित्रपथा: Citrapathā f.: Name of a river. Mentioned in the Daivata-Ṛṣi-Vaṃśa 13. 151. 21, 2.
चित्रबर्हा: Citrabarhā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 32, 13; all the rivers listed here are said to be mothers of the universe and very strong 6. 10. 35 (for citation see Atikṛṣṇā).
चित्रवती: Citravatī f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 25, 13; (for other details see above Citrabarhā).
चित्रवहा: Citravahā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 16, 13; (for other details see above Citrabarhā).
चित्रसेना: Citrasenā f.: Name of a river. Listed twice by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa (on both occasions as चित्रसेनां च निम्नगाम्); its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 16, 25, 13; (for other details see above Citrabarhā).
चित्रोपला: Citropalā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 32, 13 (for other details see above Citrabarhā).
चीरवती: Cīravatī f.: Name of a river. Described as holy (पुण्या) and chosen by the most holy persons (पुण्यतमैर् वृता) 3. 82. 61; by visiting the river and by wor-shipping gods and manes there (पितृदेवार्च-नरतः) one gets the fruit of a Vājapeya 3. 82. 61.
चुलुका: Culukā f.: Name of a river. Listed by Saṃjaya among the rivers of the Bhāratavarṣa; its water used by people for drinking 6. 10. 19, 13; (for other details see above Citrabarhā).
चैत्यक: Caityaka m., nt.: Name of a mountain and also of its peak (गिरेः शृङ्गम् 2. 19. 41). One of the five mountains shown by Kṛṣṇa to Bhīma and Arjuna which by coming very close together were as though protecting the city Girivraja in the Magadha (रक्षन्ती-वाभिसंहत्य … गिरिव्रजम्) 2. 19. 2-3; all the five mountains are described as shining (शुभाः), having high peaks (महाशृङ्गाः) and shady trees (शीतलद्रुमाः), and of very solid forms (संहिताङ्गाः); they were fully covered by the forests of Lodhra trees which were fragrant, attractive, and whose branches were covered with flowers 2. 19. 2-4; the peak of the mountain (शृङ्ग) is described as very attractive (सुरुचिर), firm (स्थिर), very large (सुविपुल), very big (सुमहत्), old (पुरातन), always wor-shipped with garlands (अर्चितं माल्यदामैश् च सततम्), and firmly established (सु-प्रतिष्ठित) 2. 19. 17-18; Kṛṣṇa and the Pāṇḍavas ran up to the top of the mountain (चैत्यकान्तम्) and struck it with their large hands and broke it; then they saw from there the city of Magadha (Girivraja) and entered it 2. 19. 17, 19, 41.
च्यवनस्य: *Cyavanasya saraḥ nt.: Name of a sacred lake. A. Description: Attractive (रम्य), best (उत्तम) 3. 122. 5; resonant with sounds of birds (द्विजसंघुष्ट) 3. 125. 11. B. Epic event: Lomaśa showed the lake to the Pāṇḍavas (तस्य (i. e. च्यवनस्य) एतत् सरः); he advised them to perform there rites to satisfy manes and gods 3. 125. 11. C. Past events: Cyavana practised austerities near this lake 3. 122. 1; (2) King Śaryāti came to this lake with his wives and daughter Sukanyā to sport 3. 122. 5-6; (3) Cyavana entered this lake to be young again; Aśvinau entered it too; they all emerged young, of divine form and having the same appearance 3. 123. 15-17.

Cyavanasya āśramaḥ m.: An आश्रम of Cyavana. A. Location: In the west (प्रतीच्याम्) 3. 87. 1; the river Vadhūsarā which arose from the tears of Pulomā, wife of Bhṛgu, flew along the आश्रम (नाम तस्यास् तदा नद्याश् चक्रे लोकपितामहः । वधूसरेति भगवांश् च्यवनस्याश्रमं प्रति) 1. 6. 7. B. Description: Holy (पुण्य) 3. 100. 4; known (ख्यात) 3. 87. 10; resorted to by the twiceborn (द्विजनिषेवित) 3. 100. 4. C. History: Apparently Bhṛgu, father of Cyavana, also lived in the same आश्रम with his wife Pulomā; in that case the आश्रम could have been established by Bhṛgu 1. 5. 13. D. Holiness: Men obtain perfec-tion there by practising austerities even for a short period (तत्राल्पेनैव सिध्यन्ति मानवास् तपसा विभो) 3. 87. 10. E. Epic event: One of the places where Ambā bathed and practised austerities to be able to kill Bhīṣma (च्यवनस्याश्रमे चैव … आप्लावयत गात्राणि तीव्रम् आस्थाय वै तपः) 5. 187. 25, 28. F. Past events: (1) A cer-tain demon (रक्षस्) entered the आश्रम, when Bhṛgu was away; he became infatua-ted at the sight of Pulomā 1. 5. 14; the demon desired to kidnap Pulomā from the आश्रम after finding out from the fire whether she was Bhṛgu's wife 1. 5. 20, 25; (2) The Kāleya demons devoured a hun-dred ascetics living in Cyavana's आश्रम who subsisted on fruit and root (फलमूला-शनानां हि मुनीनां भक्षीतं शतम्) 3. 100. 4. [See Bhṛgor āśramaḥ]
चण्डालिकाश्रम: Caṇḍālikāśrama: Name of an आश्रम। Situated near the Kokāmukha तीर्थ; one who visits this आश्रम and bathes in the Kokāmukha tīrtha and if he subsists on vegetables and wears bark garments or rags he gets the reward of visiting the Kumārī tīrtha ten times (शाकभक्षश् चीर-वासाः कुमारीर् विन्दते दश) 13. 26. 49 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 13. 25. 52: कुमारीः कुमारीसंज्ञकतीर्थम्). [See Kumārī1, Vol. 1, p. 312]
चम्पा: Campā f.: Name of a city, also called Mālinī (12. 5. 7). A. Location: In the Aṅgaviṣaya (here called Mālinī) (प्रीत्या ददौ स कर्णाय मालिनीं नगरीम् अथ । अङ्गेषु … ॥ पालयाम् आस चम्पां तु कर्णः) 12. 5. 6-7; (जगाम चम्पाम् … तम् अङ्गराजं विषयं च तस्य) 3. 113. 15; 13. 42. 7-8, 33; river Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā) flew by Campā (तथा चम्पां समासाद्य भागीरथ्यां कृतोदकः) 3. 82. 142; 3. 292. 26. B. Description: Having the rows of Campaka trees as garland (चम्पकमालिनी) 13. 42. 16. C. Charac-teristic: Characterized as a town (पुरी) having the settlement of Sūtas (सूतविषयं चम्पाम् अभ्याययौ पुरीम् । स मञ्जूषागतो गर्भः) 3. 292. 26; also called नगरी (12. 5. 6). D. Epic events: (1) The basket in which the newly born child (Karṇa) was placed went from Aśvanadī to Carmaṇvatī and then flew to Yamunā and then along Gaṅgā to Campā 3. 292. 26; (2) Jarāsandha, defeated by Karṇa in a duel, gave him the town Mālinī in the Aṅga country; Karṇa, with the consent of Duryodhana, protected Campā (प्रीत्या ददौ स कर्णाय मालिनीं नगरीम् अथ । अङ्गेषु … ॥ पालयाम् आस चम्पां तु कर्णः  … । दुर्योधनस्यानुमते) 12. 5. 6-7. E. Past events: (1) Sage Vibhāṇḍaka, enraged at not finding Ṛśyaśṛṅga in his आश्रम, started for Campā to burn the king of Aṅgas and his country 3. 113. 15; (2) Vipula picked up the flowers having heavenly fra-grance from the place where they had fallen from the body of a divine woman (13. 42. 5-6) and went to Campā 13. 42. 16; having reached Campā he gave the flowers to his teacher Devaśarman 13. 42. 33.
चेदिपुर: Cedipura, Cedipurī, Cedirājapurī, Cedī-nāṃ purī: See Śuktimatī.
चर्मखण्डिक: Carmakhaṇḍika m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the nor-thern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (पह्लवाश् चर्म-खण्डिकाः) 6. 10. 46 (for other citation see above Govinda).
चिच्छिल: Cicchila m. (pl.): Name of a people. On the eighth day of war, the Cicchila warriors formed part of the army which, led by Bṛhadbala, stood behind Bhagadatta in the Mahāvyūha (6. 83. 5, 15) of Kaura-vas (कौसल्यो ऽथ बृहद्बलः । … चिच्छि-लैश् च समन्वितः) 6. 83. 9.
चीन: Cīna m. (pl.): Name of a people; Cīnadeśa (m. sg.) Name of the country (5. 84. 10; 12. 312. 15). A. Location: Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern म्लेच्छस् of the Bhārata-varṣa (उत्तराश् चापरे म्लेच्छा जना … ) 6. 10. 63; (तथैव मरधाश् चीनास् … ) 6. 10. 65; they lived between Badarī and Subāhu's country; Pāṇḍavas crossed their land to reach Subāhu's country (चीनांस् तुखारान् … अतीत्य दुर्गम् हिमवत्प्रदे-शम् पुरं सुबाहोर् ददृशुर् नृवीराः) 3. 174. 12; the country lay between the peak of Meru and Āryāvarta 12. 312. 15. B. The country famous for: Antelope-skins; Dhṛtarāṣṭra wanted to give Kṛṣṇa antelope-skins as gift (अजिना-नां सहस्राणि चीनदेशोद्भवानि च) 5. 84. 10; other materials: among the tributes brought for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira are mentioned woolens, blankets made from the hair of Raṅku deer (राङ्कवम्), silk, पत्तज kind of cloth, all in bundles (?कुट्टीकृतम्; Nī. on Bom. Ed. 2. 51. 27: कुटीकृतम् चित्रगुच्छाकारं कृतम्), all in large sizes, rich in colour, very soft to touch (प्रमाणरागस्पर्शाढ्यं बाह्ली-चीनसमुद्भवम्), as also other materials, soft and having the colour of lotus (कमलाभं … श्लक्ष्णम्), not made of cotton, viz. sheep-skins and soft antelope skins (वस्त्रम् अकार्पासम् आवि-कम् मृदु चाजिनम्) 2. 47. 22-23. C. Epic events: (1) When Arjuna fought with Bhagadatta in his expedition to the north before the Rājasūya, the latter was assis-ted by Kirātas and Cīnas 2. 23. 19; (2) They brought tribute for the Rājasūya, but were stopped at the gate 2. 47. 19-20; (for their tribute see above section B); at the Rājasūya they acted as servers (यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 21-22; (3) Pāṇḍavas proceeded to Subāhu's country from Badarī; on way, they had to cross the country of Cīnas 3. 174. 12; (4) Bhaga-datta's unassailable army consisted of Cīnas and Kirātas equipped with gold coloured outfit (चीनैः किरातैश् च काञ्चनैर् इव संवृतम् । बभौ बलम् अनाधृष्यम्) 5. 19. 15. D. Past events: (1) Bhīma men-tioned Dhautamūlaka, king of Cīnas, who was among the eighteen kings who extirpa-ted their kinsmen, friends and relations 5. 72. 11, 14; (2) When Śuka left the peak of mountain Meru (12. 310. 11) to go to Mithilā, he crossed countries inhabi-ted by Cīnas and Hūṇas before he arrived at Āryāvarta (स देशान् विविधान् पश्यन् चीनहूणनिषेवितान् । आर्यावर्तम् ईमं देशम् आजगाम महामुनिः) 12. 312. 15; (3) Māndhātṛ asked Indra how kings like him should govern people like Cīnas who, although they lived in country side, led the life of Dasyus; he also asked Indra the nature of their धर्म (कथं धर्-मं चरेयुस् ते सर्वे विषयवासिनः । मद्-विधैश् च कथं स्थाप्याः सर्वे ते दस्यु-जीविनः ॥ ) 12. 65. 13, 15; thereupon Indra told him their धर्म 12. 65. 17-22.
चूचुप: Cūcupa m. (pl.): Name of a people. A. Location: They belonged to the south (दक्षिणापथजन्मानः) 12. 200. 39. B. Characterization: They did not believe in Dhātṛ being the अध्यक्ष of all beings (अध्यक्षं सर्वभूतानां धाता-रम् अकरोत् प्रभुः ॥ … निरध्यक्षांस् तु कौन्तेय कीर्तयिष्यामि तान् अपि ॥ … चूचुपाः मण्डपैः सह) 12. 200. 33, 38-39; sinful, they roamed about over the earth living like dogs, crows, बलस् (?) and vultures; they did not exist in the Kṛta-yuga, but were found since the Tretā 12. 200. 41-42. C. Epic events: (1) Kṛṣṇa told Karṇa before the war that if he were to join the Pāṇḍavas, Cūcupas and many other people would lead his procession (पुरोगमाश् च ते सन्तु) 5. 138. 25; (2) On the second day of the war, Duryodhana, helped by Cūcupas and other warriors, protected the army of Śakuni 6. 47. 16: (3) On the sixth day, they were posted at the right wing of the Krauñcavyūha of the Kauravas 6. 71. 14, 20.
चेदि: Cedi(ka) m. (pl.): Name of a country and its people, often mentioned along with Kāśis, Karūṣas, Pāñcālas, and Matsyas; the people once referred to as चैद्य (5. 4. 14); the country is referred to as Janapada (4. 1. 9; 6. 10. 39), Deśa (1. 57. 7, 9), or Viṣaya (1. 57. 2); its warriors once designated as Cedika (8. 32. 34). A. Location: Mentioned by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of Bhāratavarṣa (चेदि-वत्साः करूषाश् च) 6. 10. 39, 37, 5; one of the Janapadas lying around Kuru country (परितः कुरून् । पाञ्चालास् चेदिमत्स्याश् च) 4. 1. 9. B. Capital: Śukti (पुरीं रम्यां चेदीनां शुक्तिसाह्वयाम्) 14. 84. 2; it is referred to as Cedirājapurī 3. 62. 20, or as Cedipura 2. 40. 14, or as Cedipurī 3. 65. 6. C. Description: (1) Country: holy (पुण्य) 1. 57. 8; gentle (सौम्य) 1. 57. 8; delightful (रम्य) 1. 57. 2; 4. 1. 9; worth accepting (ग्रहणीय) 1. 57. 2; firmly established (सुस्थिर) 1. 57. 8; called the udder of the land (ऊधः पृथिव्या यो देशः) 1. 57. 7; hence rich in food (बह्वन्न) 4. 1. 9; having ample corn, wealth, jewels (धनधान्यवन्त्) 1. 57. 8; (धनरत्नादिभिर् युतः) 1. 57. 9; the land was full of wealth (वसुपूर्णा च वसुधा) 1. 57. 9; thus having all enjoyable qualities of (good piece of) land (भोग्यैर् भूमिगुणैर् वृतः) 1. 57. 8; suitable for cattle (पशव्य) 1. 57. 8; excelled other countries (अत्यन्यान् एष देशो हि) 1. 57. 9; to be well protected (स्वारक्ष्य) 1. 57. 8; (2) People: They were virtuous, followed their धर्म, were quite satisfied; they did not utter a lie even in joke, were obedient to fathers, intent on doing good to teachers; cows were never put to yoke, the lean ones were nourished; all वर्णस् lived within the limits of their धर्म (धर्मशीला जनपदाः सुसंतोषाश् च साधवः । न च मिथ्याप्रलापो ऽत्र स्वैरेष्व् अपि कुतो ऽन्यथा ॥ न च पित्रा विभज्यन्ते नरा गुरुहिते रताः । युञ्जते धुरि नो गाश् च कृशाः संधुक्षयन्ति च) 1. 57. 10-11 (Nī. on Bom. Ed. 1. 63. 11 takes गाः as mas. pl. and explains संधु-क्षयन्ति as पुष्टान् कुर्वन्ति); the most excellent among them knew eternal धर्म; virtuous and, distinguished they lived according to the ancient धर्म (चेदयश् च महाभागा धर्मं जानन्ति शाश्वतम्; चेदयो ये विशिष्टाः । धर्मं पुराणम् उपजीवन्ति सन्तो … ) 8. 30. 61-62; (3) Warriors: brave (शूर) 7. 8. 27; 7. 101. 68; 8. 8. 19; honoured by the brave (शूरसंमत) 8. 40. 62; distinguished chariot-fighters (महारथ) 6. 102. 17; 8. 40. 2, 51; 8. 56. 23; born in noble families (कुलपुत्र) 6. 102. 17; they were willing to die but not turn away from the battle-field (तनुत्यजः । अपरावर्तिनः सर्वे) 6. 102. 17; (चेदीनाम् अनिवर्तिनाम्) 8. 32. 80; their banners made of gold (सुवर्ण-विकृतध्वज) 6. 102. 17. D. Epic events: (1) At the birth of Arjuna, a noncorporeal voice declared that Arjuna would bring under his control Cedis, Kāśis and Karūṣas 1. 114. 31; (2) King Pauṇḍraka was known as पुरुषोत्तम among the Cedi people (पुरुषोत्तम-विज्ञातो यो ऽसौ चेदिषु दुर्मतिः) 2. 13. 17; (3) Yudhiṣṭhira installed the son of Śiśupāla as the ruler of the Cedi country (चेदीनाम् आधिपत्ये) 2. 42. 31; (4) Dru-pada suggested to Pāṇḍavas to send messen-gers (5. 4. 25) to different kings to seek their help, one of them being Dhṛṣṭaketu, the king of the Cedis (चैद्याधिपतिर् एव च) 5. 4. 14; (5) Dhṛṣṭaketu joined the Pāṇḍavas with an अक्षौहिणी army of Cedi warriors 5. 19. 7; 5. 22. 24; 5. 56. 33; 5. 70. 14; 5. 142. 3; 5. 197. 2; Dhṛṣṭa-ketu was the lone principal warrior from the Cedis who joined the Pāṇḍavas (एको ऽपसृत्य चेदिभ्यः पाण्डवान् यः समाश्रि-तः । ध्र्ष्टकेतुम् तम् … ) 7. 9. 39; (6) Others joined the Kauravas (चेदयश् चापरे वङ्गा माम् एव समुपाश्रिताः) 7. 23. 7; (7) Cedis mentioned among those who would consecrate Karṇa as the king if he were to join the Pāṇḍavas 5. 138. 17; (8) Kuntī grieved at the prospect of Cedis fighting against Bhāratas (चेदिपाञ्चालाः … भारतैर् यदि योत्स्यन्ति किं नु दुःखम् अतः परम्) 5. 142. 12; (9) Before the war Duryodhana boasted that, helped by his army, he would fight against Cedis and all those on the side of Pāṇḍavas 9. 2. 23; (10) On the first day of the war, Bhīṣma's banner was seen moving in the army of the Pāṇḍavas consisting of warriors from Cedi, Kāśi and Karūṣa countries 6. 45. 3-4; (11) On the second day, Bhīṣma showered them with arrows 6. 48. 9; (12) On the same day Bhīma faced the attack of Ketumant helped by the Cedis (on the side of the Kauravas) (भीम-सेनः … आर्छद् … केतुमन्तं च … आया-तं सह चेदिभिः) 6. 50. 5; Śrutāyu and Ketumant attacked Bhīma surrounded by Cedis (on the Pāṇḍavas' side) 6. 50. 6, 8; Cedis were outnumbered by Kaliṅgas and Niṣādas; they fought bravely but, finally, they returned abandoning Bhīma; even though Cedis deserted Bhīma (संणि-वृत्तेषु चेदिषु) he continued to fight with Kaliṅgas 6. 50. 13-16; (13) On the third day, Cedis, led by Dhṛṣṭaketu, stood on the right side of the Ardhacandravyūha of Pāṇḍavas 6. 52. 10, 13; towards the end of the same day, Cedis and others raised a loud roar with delīght due to the great havoc caused by Arjuna 6. 55. 126; (14) On the fourth day, Cedis occupied the same place in the Vyūha as on the previous day 6. 56. 11; (15) On the ninth and tenth day, Bhīṣma killed fourteen thousand Cedi, Kāśi and Karūṣa warriors along with their horses, chariots and elephants (सवाजि-रथकुञ्जराः) 6. 102. 17-18; 6. 112. 73; (16) On the tenth day, Śikhaṇḍin, along with Cedis and Pāñcālas, attacked Bhīṣma 6. 111. 26; they rushed at Bhīṣma, produc-ing noise, riding chariots and horses and elephants; some of them were foot-soldiers (ततः हिलहिलाशब्दः꣡ क्षणेन समपद्यत । मत्स्यपाञ्चालचेदीनाम् … ते वराश्वरथव्रातैर् वारणैः सपदाति-भिः) 6. 113. 47-48; on the seventeenth day of war, Kṛṣṇa, while recounting the past incidents, reminded Arjuna that Cedis and others, protected by him, had reduced the army of the enemies; but Bhīṣma succeeded in putting many of them to death 8. 51. 6, 27, 32; (17) On the ele-venth day, Dhṛtarāṣṭra feared that Dhṛṣṭa-dyumna, helped by Cedis and others, had killed Droṇa 7. 8. 27; (18) On the twelfth day, seeing Yudhiṣṭhira runn-ing away from Droṇa, Cedis, Kārūṣas and others attacked Droṇa; Droṇa defeated them repeatedly 7. 20. 18, 23; Droṇa's arrows put Cedis, Kekayas into utter dis-order; they were carried away like small boats by the strong current of the river (सिन्धोर् इव महौघेन ह्रियमाणान् यथा प्लवान्) 7. 21. 7-8; Droṇa killed many Cedis 7. 31. 39; (19) The king of Cedis showering arrows, kept Ambaṣṭha away from Droṇa 7. 24. 47; (20) Subhadrā blamed Cedis and others neglecting Abhi-manyu's fall in battle 7. 55. 13; (21) On the fourteenth day, Alambusa Rākṣasa made a river of blood flow carrying away many Cedis and others 7. 83. 30; Kṛtavar-man defeated Cedis and others 7. 90. 47; Cedis and others, delighted, attacked Droṇa crying ‘kill Droṇa, kill Droṇa’; they made effort with all their might to kill Droṇa; Droṇa killed them, specially their chiefs, with arrows; seeing them diminished Pāñcālas trembled 7. 101. 50-53; Duryodhana struck Cedis with many sharp arrows 7. 128. 23; (22) During the night war (fourteenth-fifteenth day), distinguished archers among Cedis (चेद-यश् च महेष्वासा … ) attacked Droṇa; he defeated them and killed them 7. 161, 30, 32, 35; (23) On the fifteenth day, the crown prince of Cedis (युवराजश् च चेदीनाम्) struck Aśvatthāman with five arrows; he killed the prince, who was dear to Cedis (चेदिप्रियम्), along with his horses and the chariot-driver 7. 171. 56, 65; (24) On the sixteenth day, Cedis and others rushed at the Kaurava army 8. 8. 19; they also attacked Karṇa 8. 21. 26; (25) On the seventeenth day, Cedis and others fought fiercely with the Kaurava army; Duryodhana offered protection to Karṇa while he was fighting with Cedis and others; in their renewed battle with Karṇa, three hundred Cedi chariot-fighters, who did not turn back, lost their life (स रथांस् त्रिशतान् हत्वा चेदीनाम् अनिवर्तिनाम्) 8. 32. 15, 20, 43, 80; in the meantime Karṇa had also killed hundreds and thousands of ordi-nary Cedi fighters (चेदिकान् अवधीद् वीरः शतशोऽथ सहस्रश्हः) 8. 32. 34; when Yudhiṣṭhira, defeated and humiliated by Karṇa in a duel, retreated from the battlefield, Cedis and other warriors followed him 8. 33. 41; when Cedi and Pāñcāla armies were engaged with Karṇa, he destroyed them; then they began to flee 8. 43. 24, 26-28; in his fight with Karṇa, Bhīma was accompanied by Cedis; Karṇa killed great Cedi chariot-fighters (महारथान्) and many others, respected by brave (शूरसंमताः) 8. 40. 1, 2, 51, 62, 68; 8. 45. 41; Śalya drove Karṇa's chariot towards Cedis, Pāñcālas and Karū-ṣas; Karṇa killed Pāñcalas and the great chariot-fighters (महारथान्) of the Cedis; Cedis and others, although being killed by Karṇa, continued to shoot arrows at Karṇa; Karṇa killed more than a hundred Cedi horse-riders (सादयः क्रोधाच् चेद-यश् च परःशताः) 8. 56. 9. 23-24, 49; (26) On the last day of the war, Śalya wanted to show his valour to Pāñcālas, Cedis and the rest 9. 6. 13; he killed twenty five Cedi warriors 9. 11. 53; during the war of eighteen days, all Cedis were killed (चेदयश् च निषूदिताः) 9. 1. 30; 15. 44. 34; (27) The Aśvamedha horse, wander-ing at will, reached the beautiful town of the Cedis called Śukti (आससाद पुरीं रम्यां चेदीनां शुक्तिसाह्वयाम्) 14. 84. 2. E. Past events: (1) King Vasu Upari-cara, a Paurava, accepted the rulership of the Cedi country as directed by Indra (स चेदिविषयं रम्यं वसुः पौरव-नन्दनः । इन्द्रोपदेशाज् जग्राह ग्रहणी-यं महीपतिः ॥ ) 1. 57. 2, (वस चेदिषु चेदिप) 1. 57. 9; while living in Cedi country, he protected the earth according to धर्म 1. 57. 27; (2) Bhīma mentioned king Sahaja of Cedis and Matsyas among the eighteen kings who were responsible for the destruction of their kinsmen, friends and relatives (अष्टादशेमे राजानः … । ये समुच्चिच्छिदुर् ज्ञातीन् सुहृदश् च स-बान्धवान् ॥ … सहजश् चेदिमत्स्यानाम्) 5. 72. 11, 16. F. Certain persons referred to as the king of the Cedis or as the foremost among the Cedis: चेदिप: (1) Dhṛṣṭaketu 3. 13. 2; 5. 78. 14; 5. 81. 31; 6. 91. 23, 39; 7. 34. 3; (2) Vasu Uparicara 1. 57. 9; चेदिपति: (1) Dhṛṣṭaketu 3. 120. 25; 5. 49. 43; 5. 168. 9; 11. 25. 20; (2) Vasu Uparicara 1. 57. 23, 27; 13. 116. 54; (3) Śiśupāla 2. 35. 5; 2. 37. 13, 15; 2. 39. 20; 2. 41. 1, 24; 2. 42. 22; 2. 49. 6; 5. 22. 24, 27; (4) Subāhu 3. 65. 33; चेदिपुंगव: (1) Dhṛṣṭaketu 11. 25. 18; (2) Śiśupāla 2. 36. 15; 2. 37. 9; चेदिराज्: (1) Dhṛṣṭaketu 3. 23. 47; 5. 56. 8; 6. 43. 75; (2) Śiśupāla 2. 35. 27; 2. 41. 4; 2. 42. 1; चेदिराज: (1) Dhṛṣṭa-ketu 5. 168. 8; 6. 43. 37; 6. 112. 23; 7. 24. 47; 7. 82. 15; 7. 101. 38; 11. 25. 21, 22; (2) Śiśupāla 2. 26. 12, 14; 2. 33. 32; 2. 35. 14; 2. 37. 12; 2. 39. 18; 2. 41. 24; 2. 42. 16, 22; 7. 10. 13; 7. 155. 29; 7. 156. 2, 5, 21; (3) Subāhu 3. 61. 125; 3. 62. 18; चेदिवृष: Śiśupāla 2. 26. 13; चेदीनाम् अधिपतिः: Dhṛṣṭaketu (चेदीनाम् आधिपत्ये) 5. 42. 31; चैद्याधिपति: Dhṛṣṭaketu 5. 4. 14; चेदीनाम् ईश्वरः प्रभुः: Vasu 14. 94. 22; चेदीनाम् ऋषभः: Dhṛṣṭaketu 5. 19. 7; 7. 22. 16; 7. 81. 9; 7. 101. 25; चेदीनां प्रवरो रथः: Dhṛṣṭaketu 8. 4. 80.
चेदिवत्स: Cedivatsa m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada. Listed by Saṃjaya among the northern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 68) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अत ऊर्ध्वं जन-पदान् निबोध) 6. 10. 37, 5; (चेदिवत्साः करूषाश् च) 6. 10. 39.
चैत्रक: Caitraka, Caitraki m. (pl.): Name of a people. (1) Duryodhana saw Caitrakis and others acting very submissively towards Yudhiṣṭhira as if they were his slaves (अवार्जिता इवाभान्ति निघ्नाश् चैत्रकिकौकु-राः … युधिष्ठिरनिवेशने) 2. 46. 21; (2) They followed Kṛṣṇa's advice and hence could control their enemies and give delight to their friends (चैत्रकाश् चान्ध-काश् च … उपासीना वासुदेवस्य बुद्धिं निगृह्य शत्रून् सुहृदो नन्दयन्ति) 5. 28. 11.
चोल: Cola m. (pl.): Name of a Janapada and its people. A. Location: (1) South of Bhārata-varṣa: Listed by Saṃjaya among by the southern Janapadas (also called Deśas 6. 10. 66) of the Bhāratavarṣa (अथापरे जनपदा दक्षिणा भरतर्षभ) 6. 10. 58, 5; (कौकुट्टकास् तथा चोलाः) 6. 10. 58; called Janapadas also in चोलाः पाण्ड्याश् च भारत । एते जनपदा राजन् 6. 46. 50; mentioned along with Draviḍas 3. 48. 22; (2) However, Arjuna is said to have con-quered them in his expedition to the north before Rājasūya (धनंजयः । प्रययाव् उत्तरां दिशम्) 2. 24. 1; (ततः सुह्माश् च चोलांस् च … प्रामथत् कुरुनन्दनः) 2. 24. 20. B. Epic events: (1) Arjuna defeated them before Rājasūya 2. 24. 20; (2) They and their kings acted as servers in the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira (यत्र सर्वान् महीपालाञ् … सचोलद्रविडा-न्ध्रकान् … यज्ञे ते परिवेषकान्) 3. 48. 18; (3) On the second day of war, they were stationed at the right wing of the Krauñcāruṇavyūha of the Pāṇḍavas (चोलाः  … दक्षिणं पक्षम् आश्रिताः) 6. 46. 50, 39; (4) While recounting the past victories of Kṛṣṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra mentioned his victory over the Colas 7. 10. 17.
